categories.description: Display-only topical labels, e.g. ai and bots. The source label (first-party, partner, or community) goes in the index entry, not here.

layout.description: router generates one function that dispatches on URL path; separate deploys each operation as its own function.

required.description: Written as the variable's required in neon.ts. true (the default) fails neon deploy and neon dev while it is unset; false lets both run without it; "default-branch" requires it only when deploying the project's default branch.

source.description: Module path relative to this template.json.

route.description: Router layout: the URL path. Defaults to /<id>.

slug.description: Separate layout: the Neon function slug.

agent.description: Coding-agent tooling the CLI sets up in the project after scaffolding. Nothing here is bundled: skills go through the skills CLI and MCP servers through the add-mcp CLI, both run with npx for the agents the user picked; npm CLIs are installed globally with npm install -g, only after the user confirms.

source.description: Passed to `skills add`: owner/repo or an https Git URL. Local paths are not allowed.

skills.description: Skill names inside source, each passed as --skill.

recommended.description: false leaves it unchecked in the picker and skips it under -y.

mcpServer.description: A remote server (url) or a local stdio server (command), never both.

name.description: Key written into each agent's MCP config. neon is reserved: neon init and neon mcp own that entry.

recommended.description: false leaves it unchecked in the picker and skips it under -y.

url.description: Remote server endpoint. No credentials in the URL and no $: agents expand ${...} in their configs.

headers.description: Remote servers only. Each is passed as --header 'Key: Value'.

prefixItems.description: A bare executable on PATH, such as npx or uvx.
add-mcp splits its target on spaces, so the first argument cannot contain one.

command.description: Local stdio server, as argv: an executable and its arguments, none containing $. A command runs on the user's machine whenever their agent starts, so third-party templates need explicit consent for it.

env.description: Local stdio servers only. Each is passed as --env KEY=VALUE.

cliTool.description: A command-line tool the project's agents should be able to run: an npm package the CLI installs into the project (npm), or a system tool the CLI only checks for (install), never both.

name.description: The executable, e.g. inngest or stripe. For npm, a bin of that package.

description.description: What an agent uses it for. Shown in the consent summary and the completion output.

recommended.description: false leaves it unchecked in the picker and skips it under -y.

npm.description: An exact name@version pin, installed globally with npm install -g when the CLI's name is not already on PATH.

minVersion.description: System tools only: the oldest version that works. The CLI runs `<name> --version` and compares the first x.y.z it prints.

install.description: System tools only: how to install it, printed when it is missing or too old. The CLI never runs these.

headerMap.description: A literal, or literals mixed with ${NAME} placeholders. Any other $ is rejected. Neon's own templates fill placeholders from the environment or the project's .env (never NEON_*, cloud, or VCS credentials); third-party templates only from a prompt.

envMap.description: A literal, or literals mixed with ${NAME} placeholders. Any other $ is rejected. Neon's own templates fill placeholders from the environment or the project's .env (never NEON_*, cloud, or VCS credentials); third-party templates only from a prompt.
